reuse.why: Reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules and getRangeAmount, and routes every hand-written missing/number/range dispatch through one helper, but adds getWorstCaseAmount beside the existing getScheduledAmount (which already decided missing/number/range) instead of extending that helper directly.

duplication.why: Removes four inline copies of the missing/number/range dispatch; getScheduledAmount now delegates, so no logic is copied, though two overlapping public entry points remain.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getRangeAmount and getScheduledAmount, the module every server and client consumer already imports from.

scope.why: Focused on the approximate-amount rule plus the site migrations and tests; the only unrelated edit is an import reorder in api-models.ts.

maintainability.why: One definition for the worst-case rule, but the op parameter is optional, so a caller that forgets it silently gets the old behaviour, and callers now pass a positional `false` to reach the op argument of getScheduledAmount.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed sites call the shared getWorstCaseAmount/getScheduledAmount; nothing goes around them.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount delegates to getWorstCaseAmount rather than repeating its logic; the removed inline ternaries are replaced, not reshaped.

one_place.where: getWorstCaseAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts; schedule-template, forecast-schedules, schedules/app (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule), computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, api-models and Balance.tsx all reach it (directly or through getScheduledAmount with op).
